title: Finite coherent factorization of a cohomological epimorphism from a perfect coefficient module
statement:
Let $D$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], let $D\to A$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, and let $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}D$ be separated and of finite type [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-morphism-conventions]. For a commutative $D$-algebra $E$ with a specified map $E\to A$, put $Y_E=Y\times_D\operatorname{Spec}E$ and let $\pi_E:Y_A\to Y_E$ be the projection [def-pc-fibre-product]. Use $\mathcal B$, $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal B)$, $\Phi_E$, $\widehat K$, $U$, perfection over $\mathcal B$, and the specified action arrow $\nu_E$ of [def-sfb-dg-coefficient-realization]. Let $H$ be perfect over $\mathcal B$, let $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_{Y_A})$ [def-pc-derived-category], let $u:H\to\widehat K$ be a morphism in $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal B)$, and let $m\in\mathbf Z$. Suppose that the morphism of sheaves $H^i(Uu):H^i(UH)\to H^i(U\widehat K)$ is surjective for every $i\ge m$.

There exist a commutative finite type $D$-algebra $E$ with a factorization $D\to E\to A$, an object $G\in D(\mathcal O_{Y_E})$ with bounded coherent cohomology [pqf-def-coherent], a morphism $\gamma:G\to R\pi_{E*}K$ in the ordinary scheme module-derived category [def-pc-derived-direct-image], and a morphism $\sigma:H\to\Phi_E(G)$ in $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal B)$ such that
$$\nu_E(\gamma)\circ\sigma=u,$$
and $H^i(U\sigma):H^i(UH)\to H^i(U\Phi_E(G))$ is surjective for every $i\ge m$. No injectivity of $H^i(Uu)$ is assumed, and no flatness of the coefficient maps or relative pseudo-coherence of $K$ is assumed.

source.place: Agent-formulated cohomological-epimorphism finite-factorization prerequisite for the unnumbered Kiehl assertion following Tag 0CSD (lemma-flat-proper-pseudo-coherent-direct-image-general). This statement is NOT asserted in that paragraph. WANTED: Kiehl (1972), Ein Descente-Lemma und Grothendiecks Projektionssatz fuer nichtnoethersche Schemata, Math. Ann. 198, pp.287--316, finite coherent factorization in the direction H to coefficient model to ordinary target, retaining surjectivity above a cutoff. Replaces the false reverse-arrow approximation in the returned delivery.

proof.text: For the empty open and every choice of $H,K,u,m$, take $E=D$, $G=0$, $\gamma=0$, and $\sigma=0$. All sheaves on that open and its coefficient base changes are zero, so the factorization equation and all surjectivity requirements hold. Thus the uniform assertion used below also holds on the empty open.

source.place: Tag 08DR (lemma-induction-principle), separated-open induction; agent assembly with the separately stated affine and two-open factorization inputs.

proof.text: The scheme $Y$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated because it is separated and finite type over an affine scheme; it is also separated as a scheme. For each quasi-compact open $W\subseteq Y$, its inclusion is quasi-compact: its inverse image of any affine open $T\subseteq Y$ is $W\cap T$, which is quasi-compact by the intersection lemma. Thus $W\hookrightarrow Y$ is of finite type, and composition makes $W\to\operatorname{Spec}D$ finite type. Its separatedness follows directly by restricting the diagonal of $Y/\operatorname{Spec}D$. The same facts apply to finite unions and intersections of quasi-compact opens.

source.place: Tag 08DR (lemma-induction-principle), separated-open induction; agent assembly with the separately stated affine and two-open factorization inputs.

proof.text: For a quasi-compact open $W$, let $P(W)$ be the uniform assertion $\mathscr P(W)$ of the locality lemma: for every perfect source $H'$, every ordinary target $K'$, every integer $r$, and every $u':H'\to\widehat {K'}$ surjective on underlying cohomology in all degrees $i\ge r$, there is the displayed finite coherent factorization with first factor surjective in those degrees. These objects are arbitrary on $W$, not restrictions of the original $H,K,u$. The coefficient construction on $W$ is $\mathcal B_W=\mathcal O_W\otimes_D R_A$ with its specified action arrow. If $W$ is affine, write $W=\operatorname{Spec}S$. Step 2 and the affine-pair criterion show that $S$ is a finite type $D$-algebra. For each such $H',K',u',r$ the affine factorization lemma applies, including its surjectivity hypothesis. It gives $P(W)$ after universal generalization.

source.place: Tag 08DR (lemma-induction-principle), separated-open induction; agent assembly with the separately stated affine and two-open factorization inputs.

proof.text: Let $O$ be quasi-compact open and $V$ affine open in $Y$, and assume $P(O)$, $P(V)$ and $P(O\cap V)$. The intersection is quasi-compact by quasi-separatedness. These are exactly the three UNIFORM premises of the two-open locality lemma, so its conclusion is $P(O\cup V)$. In particular, the premises apply to every admissible auxiliary perfect source, ordinary target and surjective arrow on the smaller opens, not only to restrictions of the original arrow. This invokes the uniform locality assertion, rather than combining three unrelated witnesses for fixed data.

source.place: Tag 08DR (lemma-induction-principle), separated-open induction; agent assembly with the separately stated affine and two-open factorization inputs.

proof.text: Apply the separated-open induction principle to this uniform property $P$ on the qcqs scheme $Y$. Step 3 supplies every affine case and step 4 supplies its union implication with the intersection premise. Since $Y$ is separated and quasi-compact, it gives $P(Y)$. Now specialize its universal quantifiers to the originally supplied $H,K,m,u$; their required surjectivity is precisely the hypothesis of the item. The resulting $E,G,\gamma,\sigma$ satisfy the ordinary scheme-derived type of $\gamma$, the equation $\nu_E(\gamma)\circ\sigma=u$, and surjectivity of $H^i(U\sigma)$ for every $i\ge m$, as required.

source.place: Tag 08DR (lemma-induction-principle), separated-open induction; agent assembly with the separately stated affine and two-open factorization inputs.
